output.brief: The gap is mostly a tenure effect, not a location effect. Promotion policy requires 18 months in level. Only 32% of remote staff meet that, against 74% of office staff, because remote hiring only opened widely in July 2024 and most remote staff are recent hires. Among eligible people, the rates are about the same: office 21.1%, remote 20.0%. Nomination rates (28.6% vs 28.2%) and approval rates (74% vs 71%) are also similar. Remote staff don't leave more often, and the gap shows up in every job family, so neither attrition nor job mix explains it. Caveat: only 110 remote staff are eligible, so a real difference of a few points can't be ruled out. Visibility and stretch-work differences are plausible (managers' comments) but unmeasured. Don't announce the three-day office rule. It targets the wrong cause, and it would hit about 180 staff hired on home-based contracts who live far from an office. Instead, report promotion rates for eligible staff only, and re-check this at the FY2027 cycle. Meanwhile, collect data on stretch-assignment allocation, and tell remote staff how the promotion criteria work.
